facts.fact: Tasdjil, the digital civil registration solution built by Technidev for ANATS with UNICEF support in 2022, registers births in civil-status offices inside hospitals, for children born in the maternity or coming for vaccination, and issues the birth act with a national identification number within 20 minutes, per ANATS's director general.

As at 16 November 2023, six hospitals in N'Djamena and twelve provincial and district hospitals had Tasdjil civil-status offices (Guichets Uniques d'Enregistrement des naissances), the first opened in August 2022; a seventh in the capital, 32 provincial and district sites and 21 others were announced by ANATS. No total of civil-status offices is given.
ANATS's director general describes registration through the technological solution as a pilot phase ('phase pilote'), operational in six N'Djamena hospitals since 2022.
Tasdjil was developed by the NGO Technidev for the state agency ANATS, with UNICEF support, and its N'Djamena campaign was launched by the Ministry of Public Health and Prevention with ANATS.

ANATS's director general says the digital registration of births by health staff comes after validation of the roadmap for accelerating universal birth registration in Chad by 2030; the roadmap's date and cost are not given.
The universal birth registration campaign for N'Djamena, called Tasdjil, was officially launched on 16 November 2023, with ANATS announcing further hospital offices to open by the end of the year.

note: No 'made' fact is taken: the document says the record is made at the hospital office at registration, in a solution that works without internet and issues the national identification number, but does not say whether the record is held in a national register or stays at the office. The offices are hospital-based, not commune or sub-prefecture offices. UNICEF's deputy representative says parents have waited more than five months for acts ANATS has yet to deliver.
